title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-09-16
content:
Serving Runtime — Weekly Update (kernel, KV cache, batching) — 2026-09-16

TL;DR:
- Kernel team landed the new fused attention microkernel (PR#842) on staging; p50 inference latency improved ~6% on 8K context for mixed-precision runs.
- KV cache: prototype eviction policy (lru+segmented) reduces memory tail but we still see periodic spikes due to long-lived sessions. Investigating snapshotting to disk for inactive sessions.
- Batching: continuous-batching rollout to a subset of low-latency customers showed 12% token/sec improvement with <2% p95 latency regression. We will expand with throttling safeguards.

Highlights / Wins:
- Fused attention microkernel merged to staging (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842). Early perf: p50 -6%, p95 ~unchanged for seq_len<=2048; larger contexts show 4-9% wins depending on quantization.
- KV cache segmented-LRU prototype reduced median memory per session by ~18% in internal load tests (JIRA-SRV-2412).
- Canary for continuous batching on the eu-west region processed 3M tokens/day with stable tail latency after policy tweaks.

Metrics snapshot (canary/staging):
- Model: redwood/open-medium-8k (quantized int8)
- p50 latency (seq 1024): 48ms (was 51ms)
- p95 latency (seq 1024): 210ms (no significant change)
- Average batch size: 6.2 tokens per request (after batching policy change)
- Token throughput (canary): +12% vs baseline
- KV cache memory: median/session 28MB -> 23MB (prototype)

Kernel Work (owner: Ethan Kim):
- What landed:
  - Fused attention microkernel (SIMD+tiling) in PR#842. Targeted to GPUs with compute capability >= X and new cu/kernels. Optimized for mixed-precision paths.
  - Kernel selector heuristics updated to prefer fused kernel for seq_len>=512 when model .arch == 'decoder' and runtime.quant==int8.
- What’s in progress:
  - Autotuner improvement: incorporate per-device sparse occupancy metrics (blocked on infra metric export — infra task assigned).
  - Fallback stability tests: a flaky case observed for batch_size=1 + beam-search; reproducer added (tests/kernel/repro_beam_1).
- Blockers / risks:
  - New microkernel triggers a rare register-pressure OOM on some older GPU drivers (NVIDIA 530.x). Need QA + driver pinning strategy for Dedicated.
  - CI perf-suite timeouts slowing iteration; plan to shard perf CI across 3 machines.

KV Cache (owner: Aisha Patel):
- Prototype: segmented LRU with hot/cold buckets to keep long-lived prefixes in a compact structure. Reduces memory churn for chatty sessions.
- Observations:
  - Memory spikes still occur when many long-lived sessions concurrently write large prefixes (>64k tokens).
  - Snapshot-to-disk design: serialize inactive session segments to fast local NVMe; eviction becomes "cold -> disk -> evict." Works in sim; integration tests next.
- Next steps:
  - Implement async snapshot writer (non-blocking) and metrics to track snapshot cycles.
  - Evaluate KMS/ACL implications for disked prefixes (security review flagged in confluence page).

Batching & Routing (owner: Marco Ruiz):
- Continuous batching rollout: enabled for route "chat-light" on eu-west canary. Key change was adaptive-window with latency target 150ms.
- Results: +12% throughput, p95 increased by 1.8% — acceptable for low-cost tier.
- Policy changes:
  - Add throttle-by-available-queue: prevents batching from growing unbounded during load spikes.
  - Introduced batch-weight concept: weight = request_token_estimate * priority_multiplier; scheduler now favors higher priority.
- Open questions:
  - How to reconcile batch-weight with model fairness for enterprise customers? (proposal: per-tenant share token budget — needs product signoff).

Standup notes (this week):
- Mon: Kernel perf run showed regressions for beam search config; Ethan to debug reproducer.
- Tue: KV cache prototype spike reproduced under synthetic workload; Aisha to add snapshot plan.
- Wed: Batching canary monitored during traffic surge; added throttle rule mid-week.
- Thu: Cross-team sync (runtime + infra + product) — decided to delay global rollout until driver compatibility gating is in place.
- Fri: QA smoke passed for fused kernel on staging GPUs; two driver versions flagged as incompatible.

Blockers / Risks (summary):
- Driver compatibility: older drivers cause rare OOM with new microkernel — mitigation: driver whitelist + forced fallback path for dedicated instances.
- KV cache disk snapshot needs security signoff (data residency/ACL).
- Perf CI slowness — slows kernel iteration pace.

Decisions made:
- Hold full rollout of fused kernel until we implement driver gating in the deployment pipeline (canary -> gated -> global).
- Expand continuous batching to additional low-tier regions after adding per-route throttling.
- Proceed with snapshot-to-disk prototype but require security review before turning on for any Private customers.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: stabilize fused kernel for beam-search edge-case + add repro test (JIRA-SRV-2418) — due 2026-09-23.
- Aisha: implement async snapshot writer and add metrics (JIRA-SRV-2412) — demo 2026-09-22.
- Marco: add per-route throttle config and rollout plan for 3 additional regions (JIRA-SRV-2419) — due 2026-09-24.
- Priya: coordinate security review for KV snapshot disk flow and produce a short risk memo for legal/compliance — due 2026-09-21.
- Infra: shard perf CI (assigned to infra team) — ETA 2 weeks.

Notes / TODOs (informal):
- Need a quick internal playbook for fallback when driver whitelist hits a Dedicated customer — template in ops-runbooks.
- Revisit batch-weight fairness after initial expansion; set a product meeting w/ pricing (Marco + Priya).
- Consider an opt-in debug header that forces smaller batch window for debugging customer issues in-prod.

Relevant links: PR#842 (fused attention), JIRA-SRV-2412 (kv cache proto), JIRA-SRV-2418 (kernel repro), JIRA-SRV-2419 (batching rollout). Confluence design doc: confluence.redwood/internal/serving-runtime/kvcache-design

Summary: good progress on kernels and systematic wins from continuous batching. KV cache prototype is promising but needs snapshot/disk integration and security signoff before wider rollout. Main short-term priority is fixing the kernel-driver incompatibility and getting perf CI faster to keep iteration speed up.

Meeting attendees (weekly sync): Priya Shah, Ethan Kim, Aisha Patel, Marco Ruiz, Lina Gomez (SRE), Oliver Zhang (product), QA rotation: Danica Lee.

File notes: informal weekly update; will convert to more formal release-note when fused kernel goes GA.
